# Imprimatur's rules live in their own generated file (.claude/rules/imprimatur.md), never in the…

Imprimatur's rules live in their own generated file (.claude/rules/imprimatur.md), never in the repo's AGENTS.md or rules files

Context: Imprimatur wrote its rules into the repo's AGENTS.md and .claude/rules/docs.md from templates (write-missing only). Repos then edited those files (halil-workspace), so a release's rule change (the /to-spec fix, #207) could not reach them: it had to be hand-patched in 5 files per repo. Imprimatur's, third-party and the repo's own rules were mixed.

Decision: .claude/rules/imprimatur.md, with a generated header, rewritten at each session start (process.js, SessionStart, repos with process settings). A file whose header the user removed is theirs and left alone. Templates no longer carry Imprimatur's rules; copies older releases wrote are an audit finding (IMP-DOC-008), not rewritten. The file says the repo's own rules win on conflict (Cursor: team > project > user; AGENTS.md: nearest wins).

Alternatives: (1) keep templates and patch the repo's files on update: rejected, overwrites the user's text or cannot apply to edited files; (2) rulesync/Ruler-style single source generating AGENTS.md: rejected, takes the repo's own file away from it; (3) MCP instructions only: rejected, capped at 1800 chars and not loaded by every client the same way.

Trade-off: the rules reach Claude Code only (.claude/rules); other agents get Imprimatur's MCP instructions. A session's first start after an upgrade may load the previous text (the hook writes while rules load).
